name: Russian State
alt: Supreme Ruler of the Russian State

predecessors.name: Provisional Siberian Government
predecessors.text: "the regions of Siberia": the Omsk Provisional Siberian Government (established 30 June 1918, power transferred 3 November 1918)

predecessors.name: komuch
predecessors.text: the Samara government (Komuch, set up 8 June 1918) whose People's Army was merged into the combined forces on 28 September 1918

predecessors.name: Provisional Regional Government of the Urals
predecessors.text: the Provisional Regional Government of the Urals formed at Yekaterinburg on 25 August 1918

successors.name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
successors.text: Omsk and Western Siberia (Red Army 14 November 1919), the Urals (Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk in July 1919), later Irkutsk

successors.name: Russian Eastern Outskirts
successors.text: Kolchak's decree of 4 January 1920 gave Semyonov "the whole civil and military power on the territory of Russia eastern outskirts"

ledger.x: 1918, 23 September: the Ufa Act makes the Provisional All-Russian Government "the sole bearer of the supreme power in the whole space of the Russian state".
1918, September: the Urals pass to the new state with the Ufa Conference.
1918, 3 October: Syzran abandoned to the Red Army ("October 3, 1918: Syzran was abandoned").
1918, 8 October: Samara, the Komuch capital, abandoned ("October 8, 1918: Samara was abandoned").
1918, 9 October: the government moves from Ufa to Omsk because of the Red Army's approach.
1918, October: the Volga-Ural front opens as Boldyrev organises three fronts (Western, South-Western, Siberian) and the Red Army takes the Volga bank; zone drawn from the cities the page names.
1918, 3 November: every minister of the Omsk Provisional Siberian Government signs the transfer of power to the All-Russian Government at Omsk.
1918, 4 November: the government orders all regional, national and Cossack governments in eastern Russia dissolved, concentrating authority in the Directory.
ledger.cp: regional, national and Cossack governments of eastern Russia

ledger.x: 1918, 18 November: Kolchak's coup; the Council of Ministers at Omsk "assumed full power and conferred it on Kolchak as Supreme Leader", ending the Directory; the state and its territory continue as the Russian State under the Supreme Ruler.
1918, 18 December: Kolchak orders military districts formed, among them a Far East district at Khabarovsk, but "Russian power there was almost nominal" and the Japanese corps held the ports.
1918, 21-24 December: the Siberian Army takes Kungur (21 December) and Perm (24 December) from the Reds.
1919, 14 March: the Western Army occupies Ufa.
1919, April: the Siberian Army takes Sarapul, Votkinsk and Izhevsk; the Western Army takes Belebey, Birsk, Bugulma (10 April) and Buguruslan and approaches Samara.
1919, 9 June: "The Red Army retook Ufa"; in June Red forces broke through the Urals.
1919, July: the Siberian Army "withdrew to the Trans-Urals, leaving Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk".
1919, summer: the Urals west of the Trans-Urals line (Perm, Kungur, the Udmurt towns, Orenburg approaches) pass to the Reds with the retreat.
1919, July: the Volga-Ural front ends as the Siberian Army withdraws to the Trans-Urals and the Western Army to Chelyabinsk and beyond.
1919, August-October: the 1st and 2nd Siberian armies join the Tobolsk offensive; in mid-October the Reds break through on the Tobol.
1919, 14 November: Omsk is evacuated and the Red Army takes it without serious resistance; Kolchak had left for Irkutsk on 13 November with the gold reserve.
1919, November: the Tobol-Omsk front ends with the fall of Omsk; the White forces fall back "in a disorganised mass" toward Transbaikalia.
1919, November-December: the rest of Western Siberia (Tomsk, Novosibirsk), Altai and the Steppe are lost as "the Eastern Front collapsed; remnants retreated to Transbaikalia".

1919, late December: Irkutsk comes under a leftist group that forms the Political Centre; Kolchak, held by the Czechoslovak Legion, no longer commands it (he is dismissed 4 January 1920 and handed over 14 January).

1920, 4 January: Kolchak's last decree transfers supreme power to Denikin and gives Semyonov "full military and civilian authority" in the Eastern Fringe; the buffer east of Baikal becomes Semyonov's own.

1920, 7 January: "The pursuing Red 5th Army took Tomsk on 20 December 1919... and Krasnoyarsk on 7 January 1920"; Kappel's army "was forced to find a route around the communist uprising in Krasnoyarsk".
1920, 4 January: the Russian State ends with Kolchak's last decree; Kolchak was shot at Irkutsk on 6 or 7 February 1920, the Alexander Kolchak page giving both dates.

wars.name: Eastern Front of the Russian Civil War
wars.outcome: Bolshevik victory: Ufa and the Urals lost in June-July 1919, Omsk on 14 November 1919, the Kolchak government ended 4 January 1920.

certainty.note: Civil-war fronts and the nominal Far East claim; no treaty or survey line exists.
